t: Brought to Constantinople and educated by his uncle Justin, Justinian was the power behind the throne in Justin's last years and ruled alone from 527 to 565.
His generals Belisarius and Narses won back North Africa and Italy and his forces took southern Hispania, but the long Gothic war devastated Italy and only Africa and Sicily proved lasting gains.

His codification of Roman law became the basis of civil law in many states, while his laws against pagans, Jews, Samaritans, heretics and homosexual men show the harsh side of his drive for unity of faith.
dyk: In the early 550s two monks smuggled silkworm eggs from Central Asia to Constantinople, and silk became a product of the empire itself.
ev: Justinian is crowned co-emperor on 1 April and becomes sole ruler after Justin I dies on 1 August
The first draft of the Codex Justinianeus is issued; the Neoplatonic Academy in Athens is closed
The Nika riots nearly overthrow him and end in a massacre in the Hippodrome; the Eternal Peace is made with Persia
Belisarius defeats the Vandals at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum and takes Carthage
The rebuilt Hagia Sophia is completed
Belisarius enters Ravenna, while Khosrau I breaks the Eternal Peace and sacks Antioch
Narses defeats the Ostrogoths at Busta Gallorum, where Totila is killed; Spania is founded in southern Hispania
Justinian dies and is succeeded by his nephew Justin II

f.born: Around 482, according to Procopius in the hamlet of Tauresium in Dardania; of a peasant family thought to be of Thraco-Roman or Illyro-Roman origin, nephew of the future emperor Justin I
f.died: 14 November 565, in his sleep at Constantinople, childless; buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles
f.role: Consul and commander of the army of the east from 520; nobilissimus and caesar from 525; co-emperor from 1 April 527; sole Roman emperor from 1 August 527 to 565
f.known: the Corpus Juris Civilis; the reconquest of North Africa, Italy and southern Hispania; the Hagia Sophia; the Nika riots; wars with the Sasanian Empire; enforcing Chalcedonian orthodoxy; the Plague of Justinian
